test_title: PYST 8 - SSC CHSL 2025 - English Language (Held On: 14 Nov, 2025 Shift 3)
subject: english
question:
**Select the option that expresses the given sentence in indirect voice.**

He said, "I finished my project, and I was working on a new one."

options.text: He said that he had finished his project and he was working on a new one.
He said that he had finished his project and he had been working on a new one.
He said that he finished his project and he had been working on a new one.
He said that he had been finishing his project and he had been working on a new one.

solution:
The correct answer is '2' i.e. He said that he had finished his project and he had been working on a new one.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The sentence provided is in direct speech and contains two clauses in the past tense: "I finished my project" and "I was working on a new one."
 
• When converting direct speech into indirect speech for past tense sentences, the tense of the verbs typically changes to the past perfect or past perfect continuous.
 
• "I finished my project" changes to "he had finished his project" in indirect speech because the past simple tense becomes past perfect tense.
 
• "I was working on a new one" changes to "he had been working on a new one" in indirect speech because the past continuous tense becomes past perfect continuous tense.

Correct sentence: *He said that he had finished his project and he had been working on a new one.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• In indirect speech, the pronouns and verbs are adjusted to reflect the perspective of the speaker. For example, "I" becomes "he" or "she" depending on the subject.
 
• Time expressions such as "today," "yesterday," or "tomorrow" may also change. However, in this case, there are no time expressions in the original sentence.
 
• Option 1 is incorrect because "he was working" is not the appropriate conversion for the past continuous tense in indirect speech.
 
• Option 3 is incorrect because "he finished his project" does not reflect the proper change to past perfect tense.
 
• Option 4 is incorrect because "he had been finishing his project" implies an ongoing action, which is not conveyed in the original sentence.
